event.title: US House Passes Sanctions Bill Against Russia and Iran
event.canonical_title: US House Passes Sanctions Bill Against Russia and Iran
event.summary: The US House of Representatives has passed a comprehensive sanctions and tariff bill aimed at increasing economic pressure on Russia due to its invasion of Ukraine. The legislation also includes measures targeting Iran and was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

event_overview.title: About Russia Sanctions
event_overview.subject: Russia Sanctions
event_overview.summary: The relevant legislative event is the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA), a U.S. law that created and expanded sanctions authorities concerning Iran, Russia, and North Korea. Its Russia provisions form one component of the broader U.S. Russia-sanctions framework, alongside authorities created by executive orders and other statutes.

facts.label: Legislative dates
facts.value: H.R. 3364 passed the House on July 25, 2017, passed the Senate on July 27, 2017, and became Public Law 115-44 on August 2, 2017.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: CAATSA is organized into separate titles addressing Iran, the Russian Federation, and North Korea; Title II addresses Russia-related sanctions and measures concerning terrorism and illicit financing.

facts.label: Stated purpose
facts.value: The enacted law states that it provides for congressional review and counters aggression by the governments of Iran, the Russian Federation, and North Korea.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control administers CAATSA-related sanctions; OFAC identifies CAATSA as implemented through Public Law 115-44 and Executive Order 13849.

facts.label: Relation to wider Russia sanctions
facts.value: CAATSA is not the only U.S. Russia-sanctions authority: OFAC separately lists Russian Harmful Foreign Activities and Ukraine-/Russia-related sanctions programs, among others.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights particular sanctions and maritime-enforcement developments, but does not provide a complete history of U.S. Russia sanctions; its September 2026 House-passage title should not be read as the date of CAATSA’s actual 2017 congressional passage.
